text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

- The Swiss National Bank (SNB) ackowledged on Monday that it had sent 70 shipments of Nazi gold to Spain and Portugal during World War Two, but defended the transfers as routine commercial payments. SNB board member Jean-Pierre Roth told Swiss television the central bank was acting as a clearing house for trade between Germany and Iberia.

- Swiss Federal Rail president Benedikt Weibel said in an interview that the so-called rolling highway through the Swiss Alps via the Loetschberg Tunnel may be completed in the year 2000. He said that some 500,000 trucks could be sent annually through the Alps this way.
- Swiss-Swedish technology group ABB received a 315 million Swiss francs order to build a combined power plant near Buenos Aires.
- Zurich Insurance Group plans to take over the remainder of U.S. reinsurer Zurich Reinsurance Centre Holding for $36 per share.
- Basle-based pharma and chemical giant Novartis plans to buy the remainder of U.S. technology group Systemix for $19.50 per share.
